situation: A customer orders an iced latte at a counter and asks if they can switch to oat milk, but the barista says oat milk is sold out and offers soy milk instead. The customer decides whether to take soy or keep regular milk.
A customer receives a hot americano but ordered an iced one, and tells the server about the mix-up. The server apologizes and says it will take five minutes to remake it.

Two close friends planned to meet at a café at 3, but one is stuck on the subway and will be fifteen minutes late. The friend already there says they will order first and asks what drink to get for the late one.

Two siblings stand in front of the dessert case deciding between a strawberry cake and a cheesecake to share. One thinks the cheesecake is sweeter, the other prefers the strawberry one because it is lighter.
A student asks a stranger at a crowded café if the empty seat by the outlet is taken, because their laptop battery is almost dead. The stranger says it is free and moves their bag.

A job candidate meets a department manager at a café near the office before a second interview. The manager asks about the candidate's experience and what drink they would like, while the candidate answers carefully and thanks them.

A customer asks the cashier for the Wi-Fi password and says the connection keeps dropping. The cashier explains that the password is printed on the receipt and that the signal is weak near the window.

A group organizer calls the café manager to reserve the back room for a book club of ten people on Saturday at 2. The manager explains the minimum order per person and the room's two-hour limit, and confirms the booking.

A customer arrives at a busy kimchi stew restaurant at 7 p.m. without a reservation and asks for a table for three, but the host says there is a 15-minute wait and offers a seat at the bar counter instead.
A waiter tells a customer that the galbi-tang is sold out today, so the customer compares it with the seolleongtang and decides what to order.
A customer received spicy tteokbokki instead of the cheese one they ordered and tells the server, who apologizes and offers to remake it in ten minutes.
Two close friends look at the menu at a sushi place and argue over whether to share a set for two or order separate bowls of chirashi, since one of them is very hungry.
A girl tries a bite of her older brother's jjamppong at a Chinese restaurant and finds it far too hot, so he suggests she order a sweet and sour pork instead.
Two friends finish dinner at a bunsik place and one realizes she left her wallet at home, so the other offers to pay and says she can send the money later.
A manager phones a restaurant to reserve a private room for eight people on Friday at 6:30 for a company dinner, and asks about the set course and parking.
A junior employee has dinner with the department head at a hanjeongsik restaurant and politely asks what the boss would like to eat, then mentions what a colleague recommended.

A shopper at a traditional market asks a fruit seller how much a box of strawberries costs and whether it is cheaper if she buys two boxes. The seller offers a small discount and adds a few extra strawberries.
A customer wants grilled mackerel for dinner, but the fish seller says the mackerel is sold out today. The seller suggests fresh cutlassfish instead, and the customer decides whether to take it.

A college student and his mom are walking through a market with a list of things to buy. He reminds her they still need tofu and green onions, and she says she will buy the pork first because it is better in the morning.
A shopper paid with a 50,000 won bill for vegetables, but realizes the vendor gave change for 10,000 won. She politely points it out and the vendor apologizes and corrects it.
Two friends at a market stall argue about which melon to buy for a picnic: one is bigger, the other smells sweeter. They compare them and finally pick one.

A shopper's bags are too heavy after buying rice and potatoes, so she asks a nearby delivery stall worker if they can deliver to her apartment by this evening. He tells her the fee and the delivery time.

A market association manager visits a stall to explain that a city hygiene inspection will take place on Thursday. The stall owner asks what he needs to prepare and promises to clean the display area before then.
A customer at a kimchi stall is given a sample and says it is a bit too salty for her taste. The seller tells her what other customers have said and shows her a milder kind she can try.
Two close friends are about to walk along the Han River at 6 p.m., but dark clouds are rolling in. One wants to go anyway, the other worries about getting wet and suggests a cafe instead.
A hiker on Namsan reaches a fork and can't tell which path leads to N Seoul Tower. She asks a passing walker, who explains the left path is shorter but steeper.
A man walking his puppy in the apartment park meets a neighbor, who asks the dog's name and age. The man says the puppy is four months old and still afraid of other dogs.
Two siblings have been walking around Seoul Forest for an hour. The younger one complains that her new shoes hurt and wants to sit down, while the older one wants to finish the loop first.
A junior employee runs into the company director during a morning walk around the lake near the office retreat. The director asks how he slept and invites him to join the walk before breakfast at 8.
Two coworkers walking home together after work decide whether to walk along the stream tomorrow evening. One can only go if the meeting ends by 6, so they agree to check with each other at lunch.

A visitor at Gyeongbokgung asks a guide at the information desk where the walking route starts and how long it takes. The guide explains that the route takes about 40 minutes and that the last entry is at 5 p.m.
Two old friends are walking to a market and disagree about the route. One says the main road is safer, while the other says the alley is faster because he heard it from a shopkeeper.

A traveler on the KTX from Seoul to Busan finds someone sitting in seat 7C, which is on her ticket. The other passenger checks his ticket and realizes he is in the wrong car, and she kindly helps him find the right one.

A guest calls the front desk of a hotel in Jeonju to say his bus is delayed and he will arrive around 11 p.m., not 8. The receptionist says the desk stays open all night but asks him to confirm the booking name.

At a Jeju Airport rental counter, a customer booked a small car but the staff says only an SUV is available today at the same price. The customer wonders about gas, insurance, and which one is easier to drive on narrow roads.

Two close friends on a trip in Gyeongju wake up to heavy rain, so they cannot bike around the tombs as planned. They decide between going to the museum and finding a cafe, and one of them says the weather forecast promised sun.
A tourist at Gyeongbokgung asks a stranger to take a photo of her in front of the gate. The stranger takes a few, and the tourist asks to retake one because her eyes were closed.

Two siblings at Sokcho beach realize the last bus to the express terminal leaves in twenty minutes. The older one wants to hurry, while the younger one wants to finish the fish cake they just bought, and they argue about whether a taxi is worth it.

A tour guide at the National Museum of Korea tells a group of visitors the museum closes at six, and that photos are not allowed in one room. A visitor asks where the group should gather and whether the audio guide costs extra.

At a pension in Gapyeong, a guest asks the host's help because the barbecue charcoal will not light and the meat is already out. The host says the wind is strong, so they suggest moving the grill behind the house and says they will bring a lighter.

A tourist realizes the Line 2 train they boarded at Hongdae is heading toward Sinchon, not Gangnam, and asks the passenger beside them what to do. The passenger explains they should get off at the next stop and cross the platform.
A college student notices an elderly man standing on a crowded bus and offers his seat. The man hesitates because his stop is coming soon, but the student insists.

Two close friends are on the subway to a movie that starts at 7:00, but their train is delayed and it's already 6:40. They decide whether to get off and take a taxi or keep waiting, and one worries about missing the trailers.

A rider's transit card has no balance left at the bus fare reader, and the driver says the bus can't leave until it's sorted. The rider asks if they can pay with cash, but the driver says cash is only accepted with exact change.

A brother and his younger sister are heading to their grandmother's house and compare taking the bus, which is slower but has a seat, with the subway, which is faster but crowded. The sister wants the faster one, and the brother wants to sit.

A junior employee shares a ride with his department head on the way to a client meeting and tells him the express bus is stuck in traffic. He suggests switching to the subway at the next station so they arrive by 2:00.

A commuter gets off the subway and realizes he left his umbrella on the train, so he asks the station attendant for help. The attendant says to describe it and fill in a lost-and-found form, and it may be found at the last stop.

A woman on the bus tells her coworker on a call that she'll call back, because a passenger next to her just asked her politely to keep her voice down. A coworker teases her and says what the boss told everyone about tomorrow's meeting.
A tourist comes out of Hongdae Station and can't find Exit 9, where a friend is waiting. A station attendant explains it is on the other side of the ticket gates and that they must go down one level.
A man wants bus 402 to Gangnam but is waiting at a stop where it doesn't run. A woman tells him to cross the street, and says the stop there is a bit far, so he might want to take the subway.
Two friends are late for a 2 p.m. class and can't find Building 5 on a big campus. One thinks it's behind the library, the other checks the map on their phone and disagrees.
A guest at a hotel front desk asks how to get to Gyeongbokgung Palace. The clerk compares walking (30 minutes) with the subway (10 minutes), and the guest decides based on the rain.

A customer asks the part-time worker at a convenience store where the nearest pharmacy is. The worker says the one on the corner closed at 8, so the customer should go to the 24-hour pharmacy near the station.
A man calls his younger sister to find the new cafe she picked. He is standing in front of a bank, and she tells him to walk past the flower shop and turn left at the second corner.
A job candidate arrives at a company lobby and asks the receptionist where the interview room is. The receptionist says it moved from the 7th to the 12th floor today and shows the elevator to use.

A passenger notices the taxi driver is going the wrong way to Seoul Station and complains politely. The driver says the road ahead is blocked, and the passenger asks whether the new route will be much slower.

A guest arrives at a Seoul hotel at 11 p.m. and wants to check in, but the front desk says the reservation is under a different spelling of her name. She wants her room soon and the clerk needs to confirm her passport.
A guest asks the front desk until what time breakfast is served and where the restaurant is. The clerk explains it is on the 2nd floor until 10 a.m., but weekends end at 10:30.

A guest calls the front desk at midnight because the room next door is very loud and she cannot sleep. The manager apologizes, promises to talk to them, and offers to move her to another floor if it continues.

A man at the desk is offered a choice between a cheaper room with a city view and a bigger room facing the garden for 30,000 won more. He compares them and decides, while the clerk explains the differences.

A guest tells housekeeping that the air conditioner in room 805 is not working and the room is hot. The staff member says an engineer will come in ten minutes, and the guest says he will wait in the lobby.
Two friends staying at a hotel in Jeju wake up and decide whether to go to the rooftop pool before breakfast or after. One wants to swim first, but the other is hungry, and they compromise.

Two siblings share a hotel room and one realizes she left her phone charger at the airport cafe. The other says she can use hers, but it is a different type, so they think about asking the front desk to borrow one.

A guest checking out asks the clerk to call a taxi to Incheon Airport and to keep her suitcase for an hour while she buys souvenirs. The clerk says the taxi takes about fifteen minutes and gives her a luggage tag.

A customer at a Myeongdong clothing shop tries on a jacket in size M but it feels tight in the shoulders, so she asks the clerk whether a size L is in stock. The clerk checks and says only the black one is left in L.

A shopper wants the navy sweater from the 30% off rack, but the clerk explains that the navy is sold out and only grey and beige remain. The shopper decides whether to take the grey one or wait for a restock next week.
Two close friends are at a mall choosing a dress for one of them to wear to a cousin's wedding on Saturday. One likes the blue dress, the other thinks the green one looks better with her skin tone.

A customer returns a pair of jeans bought online last week because the delivered size was 30 instead of 28. The staff member at the service desk asks for the receipt and offers an exchange or a refund.

An older sister sees her younger brother trying on a coat at a department store and tells him it is too big and that he will grow out of it only in a year. He insists he likes it and wants to buy it anyway.

A young man is buying his first suit for a job interview next Friday and asks the salesperson what color and cut look professional. The salesperson recommends a charcoal suit and says alterations take three days.

Two coworkers use their lunch break to look for a coat at a nearby store, and one worries they will be late getting back to the office at 1 PM. They decide to quickly check two shops and come back, even if they find nothing.

At a small store in Dongdaemun, a shopper tells her friend that the clerk said the shirt could be discounted if she buys two. The friend, who is thinking about whether she needs another shirt, reacts and they decide together.

A customer wants to send a 3kg box of winter clothes to her sister in the US and asks the post office clerk how long EMS takes versus regular airmail. The clerk explains the prices and she chooses the cheaper one even though it is slower.

A foreign student wants to open a savings account at the bank and has brought his passport but not his alien registration card. The teller says the card is required and he must decide whether to come back tomorrow.
An older customer's debit card was swallowed by the ATM after he typed the wrong PIN three times. The bank manager apologizes and explains that he can get a replacement card only after showing ID.
Two friends sit in the bank waiting area with number tickets, and one is annoyed that 15 people are ahead of her while her lunch break ends at 1:00. Her friend suggests using the mobile app instead.
A man goes to the post office with a notice slip because a courier missed him when delivering a package yesterday. The clerk looks it up and says it needs his ID, and he realizes he left it at home.
A woman accidentally transferred 500,000 won to the wrong account number and asks the teller what to do. The teller says the bank can contact the recipient, but it may take a few days.
A young couple meets a loan officer to ask about a housing deposit loan and compares two interest rates. The officer explains the conditions and tells them what documents to bring next week.

A teenage girl and her older brother stand in line at the post office to mail a birthday card to their grandmother. She says she forgot to buy a stamp, and he tells her grandma said she wanted a card even if it arrives late.
A new employee can't get the office printer to print her 20-page report because paper is jammed, and asks a colleague who sits nearby to show her how to fix it before a 3 p.m. meeting.

Two close coworker friends can't decide between kimchi stew and a burger for lunch because it's raining and they only have 50 minutes. One wants the place nearby, the other wants the tastier one farther away.

An employee calls her team leader at 8:40 because the subway line 2 stopped due to a signal problem, and she will arrive about 30 minutes after the 9:00 start. The leader asks whether she can still join the 9:30 meeting by phone.
Two coworkers in their thirties are packing up when their manager sends a request for a report due tomorrow morning. They grumble about staying until 9 p.m. even though they had plans for dinner.
A staff member asks the director for permission to take Friday and Monday off for a family wedding in Busan. The director asks who will cover the client call on Friday.

A junior colleague arrives at meeting room 4 and finds another team already inside, though his calendar says he booked it for 2 p.m. The other team says they were told it was theirs, so they check the booking and look for another room.

A team leader is taking an elevator downstairs for a coffee break and asks a much younger intern what he wants. The cafe is out of iced Americano, so the intern chooses between a latte and a cold brew.

A coworker tells a friend on the same team that the manager said the Thursday meeting is moved to Wednesday at 10 a.m. The friend is surprised because she has a dentist appointment then and wonders if she can attend online.
During a math lesson, Minji realizes she left her eraser at home and asks her close friend at the next desk if she can borrow one. The friend only has one left and offers to share it.
A student tells the teacher after class that she could not finish the English homework because she was sick yesterday. She asks if she can hand it in on Friday instead.
Two classmates who are close friends must pick a topic for the science presentation, either recycling or solar energy. They compare which one is easier to find pictures for and decide.
A university student arrives ten minutes late to a morning lecture because the subway was delayed. She quietly apologizes to the professor at the door and asks whether she may take her seat.
A student zoned out and missed what the teacher said about the exam date. She asks the classmate beside her, who explains that the teacher said the test is next Wednesday and to bring a black pen.

In a language class, a student asks the teacher if she can move to the front because she cannot see the whiteboard well. The teacher says one seat is free but it is next to the window and may be bright.

Two university classmates, who just met this semester, look at their midterm scores on the screen. One is surprised she did better than expected, while the other is disappointed even though she studied all week.
A graduate student finishes a presentation, and the professor asks why she chose a survey instead of interviews. She explains her reasons and says she plans to add interviews next semester.
A younger sister asks her older brother what they should order for dinner tonight because their parents are out; he wants chicken but she wants jjajangmyeon, and they have to pick one.
A teenager can't find the TV remote and asks his sibling if she has seen it, and she says she saw it under the sofa cushion this morning.
A daughter calls her mother to say that she will be home late tonight because her team meeting ran long, and her mother asks whether she has eaten yet.
A grandmother asks her grandson to help her send a photo on KakaoTalk, and he explains which button to press while she gets confused by the new update.
A father notices that his son left wet towels on the bathroom floor again and asks him to hang them up, while the son says he was in a hurry for school.
A mother and daughter discuss going to Busan to visit relatives on Saturday, comparing taking the KTX with driving and deciding what time to leave.
On Seollal morning, a grandson bows to his grandfather and wishes him good health, and the grandfather asks about his school plans for the new year and gives him pocket money.

A daughter formally tells her father that the air conditioner is making a strange noise and says a repair technician said he can come on Thursday, and the father asks whether that time works for the family.
A is stuck on the subway because of a signal delay and will be 20 minutes late to meet B at a cafe near Hongdae Station. A apologizes and B says to take the time and that they will order first.

Two close friends text about which movie to see on Saturday, a horror film at 7:00 or a comedy at 8:30. One prefers the comedy because the horror one is too scary, and they compromise on the later show.
A forgot a phone charger at B's apartment after studying together last night. A asks if B can bring it to class tomorrow, and B says they found it under the desk.
A coworker-turned-friend texts B to say sorry for missing a call during lunch because the phone was on silent. B says it's fine and asks whether A can look over a report before Friday.

A asks B, a friend they are not very close with, whether Thursday at 6:30 works for dinner at a Korean BBQ place. B has a dentist appointment until 6, so they discuss pushing it to 7:30 and agree to book it.
B texts A that it started raining and they forgot an umbrella on the way to the bus stop. A replies that there is a convenience store near the stop and says it will probably stop raining soon.
A, a junior colleague, texts B, a senior teacher mentor, to ask if B can attend A's small wedding on May 10 in Daejeon. B says they will gladly come and asks what time the ceremony begins.

A job applicant texts the HR manager B to say that a bus strike makes the 10:00 interview hard to reach and asks if it can be moved to 11:00. B says they will check with the interviewers and reply by this afternoon.
Minjun is on the subway and will be fifteen minutes late to meet his close friend at a cafe near Hongdae Station. He calls to say sorry and asks her to order him an iced americano first.

A customer calls a fried chicken shop because the delivery was supposed to arrive in 30 minutes but it has been an hour. The staff member apologizes, checks the order, and says the driver is two minutes away.
Two sisters decide on the phone where to eat dinner tonight: samgyeopsal near home or tteokbokki at the market. One has a cold, so they compare the options and pick one.
A woman calls a hair salon to book a cut and perm for Saturday afternoon. The 2 p.m. slot is taken, so the receptionist offers 4 p.m. or Sunday morning and she chooses.

An HR officer at a company calls a job applicant to confirm the interview time on Wednesday at 10 a.m. and explains what documents to bring. The applicant confirms and asks where to go in the building.

A man calls the subway lost-and-found because he left a black wallet on the Line 2 train this morning. The staff member asks what it looks like and tells him he can pick it up at Seoul Station tomorrow.
An employee calls her team leader in the morning to say she has a fever and can't come in today. The team leader tells her to rest and asks her to send a file if she can.
A teenager calls his grandmother to say he is coming to visit on Sunday. She asks if he has eaten and says what she heard from his mom about his exam, and he says he will bring fruit.

At a friend's birthday party, A is about to take a slice of the chocolate cake but B, the host, warns that it has peanuts in it. A is allergic and asks if there is anything else without nuts, so B offers a fruit tart.
At a housewarming party in Mapo, A realizes the last subway is at 11:50 and it is already 11:20. B, a new acquaintance, says the station is far and suggests A leave now or take a taxi with B.

At a company year-end party, a junior employee pours a drink for the department head and asks if he would like to say a few words before the toast. The department head agrees and says he will keep it short because the food is getting cold.

At a college reunion party, A points out a tall man by the window and asks B who he is. B says he is Minjun's older brother, who just came back from Canada, and A is surprised because he looks so different.

At a neighbor's rooftop party, a guest finds the music too loud to talk and asks the host if it can be turned down a little. The host apologizes, says people wanted dancing music, but agrees to lower it after ten.

Before a friend's wedding after-party, two colleagues in the party's entrance hall decide whether to give a cash envelope or a gift set. They compare prices and agree to give cash because the couple said they prefer it.
At a friend's game night, A has never played the card game B is dealing out and asks how to play. B explains that you can only play a card of the same color, and if you cannot, you must draw one.

At a reception after a company award ceremony, a guest asks the organizer where the coat check is and whether the buffet has vegetarian dishes. The organizer points to the lobby and says the vegetarian menu is on the second table.
Two close friends text about Saturday. Minji wants to go hiking at Bukhansan, but Joon says rain is forecast and suggests a movie in Gangnam instead.
An older sister asks her younger brother to come to their grandmother's house on Sunday, but he already promised to play soccer. They try to find a time that works for both.
A friend is meeting another at a brunch cafe in Seongsu at 11, but the subway is delayed. She calls to say she will be 20 minutes late and asks whether to order first.
Two coworkers chat on Friday afternoon. One invites the other to a picnic by the Han River on Saturday, but the other has to move apartments in the morning and can only come after 4.
A man calls a pension in Gapyeong to book a room for two nights this weekend. The owner says Saturday is full, so he must decide between Friday and Sunday or another weekend.
A neighbor in an apartment elevator mentions the Saturday flea market in the park. The other neighbor says she is thinking of going and asks what time it starts and if it is better in the morning.
An employee tells the team leader that he cannot join the Saturday company hike because his child has a school event. The leader asks if he can come to the dinner afterward instead.

In a job interview at a logistics company, the interviewer asks whether the candidate can work some weekends. The candidate explains that Saturdays are fine but he has a regular church commitment on Sundays.
A patient arrives at a clinic for a 3 p.m. appointment for a sore throat and wants to check in, but the receptionist says the insurance card needs to be shown and the form filled out first.
A patient tells the doctor she has had a fever and a cough since Monday, and that the over-the-counter medicine did not help. The doctor asks about other symptoms and says she should take a test.

Two sisters wait in a clinic waiting room because the younger one has a stomachache after eating cold noodles. The older one teases her and asks what she ate, while the younger one complains that the wait is too long.

After a visit, a patient asks the pharmacist how often to take the three pills and whether it is okay to drink coffee. The pharmacist explains to take them after meals, three times a day, and to avoid coffee.

A company manager comes in for his annual health checkup at a large hospital, and a nurse formally explains that he must fast after 9 p.m. the night before and that the results will arrive by mail in a week.

A man calls his close friend after visiting an orthopedic clinic for a sprained ankle, telling him what the doctor said about resting for two weeks. The friend reacts and suggests canceling their weekend hiking trip.

A dentist explains that a patient can either get a cheaper filling that lasts about three years or a more expensive crown that lasts longer. The patient compares the two options and decides on the crown, then asks to book the next visit.

A senior doctor makes morning rounds and formally asks a patient who had surgery yesterday how he slept and whether the pain has lessened. The patient answers respectfully that the pain is better but he still cannot eat much.
A man visits a gym for the first time and wants to sign up for a three-month membership. The front desk staff explains the price and mentions that a locker costs extra.
Two close friends arrive at the gym after work and find that every treadmill is in use. They decide whether to wait or do weights first.
A member can't find her locker key after her workout and her bag is inside. The manager asks her locker number and says a spare key can be brought in ten minutes.
A man is waiting to use the bench press and asks the person on it how many sets are left. The other person says two more sets and offers to let him alternate sets.
A trainer is leading a first personal training session and asks about the client's goals and any knee pain. The client wants to lose weight but says squats hurt a little.
An older sister tells her younger sister that the 7 p.m. yoga class is full, so they should try the 8 p.m. one. The younger sister complains that it will end too late.
A member tells the staff that the hot water in the men's shower isn't working. The staff member apologizes and says a technician will come, and suggests using the second-floor shower.

A gym manager meets a corporate client's HR director to propose a group membership for 50 employees. The director asks about discounts and operating hours, and says she needs to discuss it with her team.
Two close friends are leaving the dorm together. A sees dark clouds and asks if B checked the forecast, and B says rain is expected after lunch, so they decide to take umbrellas.
Two coworkers meet at the subway station on a humid July morning. They complain that it is hotter than last week and talk about wanting to eat cold noodles at lunch.
A tells younger sister B that the Han River picnic might be canceled because the forecast says heavy rain on Saturday. B is disappointed and suggests going to a movie if it rains.

At Incheon Airport, a traveler asks a check-in staff member why the flight to Jeju is delayed. The staff member explains that heavy snow and strong wind are causing the delay and that the next update will come in an hour.

On a freezing day, a customer orders an iced americano and the barista jokes that most people want hot drinks today. The customer says they prefer iced coffee even in winter and asks for an extra cup sleeve.

A hiking club member asks the leader whether the trip to Bukhansan can still go ahead because fog is expected in the morning. The leader says they will check again tonight and may start later if the fog is thick.

A junior employee reports to the department head that the company outdoor event may be affected by a typhoon warning. The head asks about alternatives, and the employee proposes moving it indoors next Friday.

Two neighbors meet at the apartment entrance and talk about fine dust being bad today. One says they wanted to jog but will wear a mask and walk instead, and the other says the air was better yesterday.
